# Results — Study 725 ("Eggflation")

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Can you trade the avian-flu
egg-price spike via Cal-Maine (CALM)? We test the strongest tradable version: does a
**labelled, cited, approximate USDA/BLS retail egg-price series** (a proxy for the tape,
not a live feed) *predict* CALM's forward return, and does an egg-momentum timer beat
buy-and-hold net of costs? Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Egg price | **Hardcoded, cited, approximate** monthly retail price, Grade-A large eggs, $/dozen, US city average (BLS `APU0000708111`), Jan-2015 → Jun-2026 — see [`docs/references.md`](references.md). **A PROXY, not a feed.** |
| Equity | `CALM` (Cal-Maine Foods) — largest US shell-egg producer; month-end Adj Close via yfinance, cached under `_cache/` |
| Benchmark | `SPY` (month-end Adj Close, yfinance) |
| As-of | 2026-06-30 (month-end; no partial-month bar) |
| Panel | 137 months (2015-02 → 2026-06), inner-joined egg×CALM×SPY |
| Fingerprint | `[egg, calm, spy]` → **`0c92a7548d09`** (`quantlab.repro.fingerprint`) |

> **Why a proxy, stated as a decision.** The retail egg price is a public government
> statistic, but it is *published with a ~two-week lag* and is not conveniently
> API-available in a single call. Rather than fabricate a live tape we (a) hardcode a
> small, clearly-cited, **approximate** monthly series whose *shape* — a quiet
> ~$1.30–1.80 base punctuated by three avian-flu (HPAI) spikes: **~$2.97** (Sep-2015),
> **$4.82** (Jan-2023, a record) and **$6.23** (Mar-2025, an all-time high) — is the
> load-bearing public fact, and (b) test the real, tradable equity (`CALM`) against it.
> The publication lag is the whole point: the tradable regressor is *last* month's egg
> change against *this* month's CALM return.

## Half 1 — the illusion: a strong LEVEL correlation

| relationship | value |
|---|--:|
| egg **level** vs CALM **level** (Pearson) | **+0.756** |

Two upward-drifting series over a decade correlate strongly on levels — a
spurious-regression artifact that says nothing about month-to-month *prediction*.

## Half 2 — does the egg-price CHANGE predict CALM's RETURN? (Newey-West, 6-lag)

| regression | slope | HAC *t* | tradable? |
|---|--:|--:|:--|
| same month `r_t ~ g_t` | −0.029 | **−0.38** | no (look-ahead) |
| **next month `r_{t+1} ~ g_t`** | +0.074 | **+0.93** | **yes — the real test** |
| next month + market control | +0.081 | +1.00 | yes |
| two months `r_{t+2} ~ g_t` | +0.135 | +2.02 | selected lag |

The same-month return co-movement is a *negative* whisper (−0.38), not the roaring link
the levels chart implied. The tradable next-month prediction is **t = +0.93** — nowhere
near the |t| = 2 bar. The only slope that nominally clears 2 is a *selected* lag (t+2),
which we test against a placebo next.

## Half 3 — the placebo: circular-shift null for the predictive *t*

| lag | observed *t* | placebo *p* | null 95% band |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 (tradable) | +0.93 | **0.483** | [−2.82, +2.52] |
| 2 (selected) | +2.02 | **0.111** | [−2.64, +2.38] |

The lag-1 signal sits squarely inside its noise band (*p* = 0.48). And the tempting
lag-2 **t = 2.02 fails its own placebo (p = 0.11)** — once you account for having
searched across lags, it is exactly what random time-shifts of the egg series produce.

## Half 4 — the mechanism: the STOCK leads the government print

| reverse regression | slope | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| `g_{t+1} ~ r_t` | +0.180 | **+2.03** |
| `g_{t+2} ~ r_t` | +0.271 | **+2.27** |

The *only* significant lead-lag runs backwards: CALM's return foreshadows the **next**
retail egg print (t ≈ 2.0–2.3). The equity market prices the shortage — from wholesale
egg futures, USDA flock/HPAI data and company guidance — weeks before it reaches the
supermarket shelf and the CPI table. The public number is a lagging summary, a receipt.

## Half 5 — the money test: an egg-momentum timer, net of costs

Long CALM when trailing 3-month egg momentum > 0 (acted on with a **one-month execution
lag**), cash at 2%/yr otherwise; 10 bp one-way per switch (25 switches, long 54% of
months). Sharpe is **excess of cash**, both legs.

| strategy | Sharpe | CAGR | ann. vol | max DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| egg timer (gross) | 0.64 | +13.9% | 20.4% | −20% |
| **egg timer (net 10bp)** | **0.63** | +13.7% | 20.4% | −21% |
| buy & hold CALM | 0.41 | +10.1% | 28.3% | −34% |
| **SPY** | **0.80** | +13.7% | 15.1% | −24% |

The timer *does* beat buy-and-hold CALM — but by **parking in cash** during CALM's
slumps (risk reduction), not by forecasting anything (§2–3 showed the egg print predicts
nothing). And it still **loses to a plain S&P index fund**. CALM's own CAPM profile
underlines the concentration: **β ≈ 0.05** to SPY, alpha +1.1%/mo but only *t* = 1.64 —
an idiosyncratic single-commodity bet, not a diversified premium.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic world where `r_{t+1} = 0.6·g_t + noise` (seed 725): the predictive
regression recovers **slope +0.646, t = +7.50, placebo p = 0.000**, and the timer earns
Sharpe **0.64** vs buy-hold **0.27**. The null world (β = 0) reads **t = +0.53** (flat).
The harness banks a real lead when one exists, so the real-tape `NONE` is a *true* null,
not a broken pipeline.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The tradable, next-month egg→CALM prediction is *t* = **+0.93**
  (placebo *p* = 0.48); the market-controlled slope is *t* = 1.00; the only lag that
  nominally clears 2 (*t*+2 = 2.02) **fails its placebo** (*p* = 0.11). The +0.76 level
  correlation is a spurious-regression artifact. No robust |t| ≥ 2 in the tradable
  direction.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The egg-momentum timer's net Sharpe (0.63) beats buy-hold
  CALM (0.41) by cash-parking, not signal, and **loses to SPY** (0.80). It concentrates
  single-name, three-event, one-commodity risk to *underperform* the index.
- **Already priced in? — CONFIRMED.** The reverse regression is the only significant one:
  CALM **leads** the next egg print (*t* = 2.03, lag-2 = 2.27). By the time "eggflation"
  is a headline, it is already in the stock.

> **Caveat (named, not buried).** The egg series is a **small, hardcoded, approximate**
> reconstruction of public reporting — its *spike shape* is defensible, its precise
> monthly values are not a live feed. Swapping in the exact BLS/USDA series would sharpen
> the *t*-stats but not flip the lead-lag sign: the stock leads the print, so the retail
> number cannot be a forecast of it. Nothing here says you can trade eggflation via CALM;
> several lines say the market beat you to it.
